subject: society
topic: Why your sense of personal agency is being systematically eroded by automation
angle: While algorithmic management is predominantly used for control and is linked to burnout and technostress, specific types of automated decision support can actually improve worker self-efficacy and satisfaction.
title: The Erosion of Personal Agency

hooks.text: Does your software make you more capable?
You think automation takes your power. It can actually give it back.
You are letting a system decide how you feel about your work.
A blue light flickers on a grey desk.
Algorithmic management is a tool of control.

reveal.headline: Automation can increase your sense of self-efficacy.
reveal.body: While systems are often used for control, specific designs like support-after-processing can improve worker satisfaction and confidence.

explain.headline: The duality of algorithmic management.
explain.body: Companies mostly use these systems to control workers, leading to burnout and data opacity. However, the technology also shapes the autonomy and value workers find in their roles.

matters.headline: Your autonomy is being reshaped.
matters.body: That may be why you feel both more capable and more exhausted at work. The way a system is built determines whether it enables you or manages you.

example.headline: The software prompt.
example.body: You sit at your desk and a notification appears. It suggests a choice for a pending task. You click to accept the help provided by the machine.

question.headline: Is the tool helping you or replacing your judgment?

claims.text: Workers in the support-after-processing group showed a steeper increase in self-efficacy in personnel selection compared to other groups.
claims.quote: Furthermore, participants in this group showed a steeper increase in self-efficacy in personnel selection compared to the other groups.

claims.text: Algorithmic management is shaped by, as much as it shapes, the autonomy and value to workers.
claims.quote: Second, we argue that algorithmic management is shaped by, as much as it shaping, the autonomy and value to workers.

claims.text: Companies have mostly used algorithmic systems in a controlling manner, rather than using them to enable workers.
claims.quote: Based on the reviewed literature, we claim that so far, companies have mostly utilized algorithmic systems in a controlling manner, neglecting the technology’s enabling potential in organizing.

claims.text: Satisfaction with the decision was higher for the support-after-processing group.
claims.quote: Results showed that satisfaction with the decision was higher for the support-after-processing group.

claims.text: Algorithmic management in the platform economy is linked to growing technostress, data opacity, and burnout.
claims.quote: The review uncovers growing technostress, data opacity, and burnout, along with a rising resistance from workers through forms of algo-activism.

verdict: The evidence shows a complex duality where algorithmic management often functions as a tool of control, yet its specific design can either diminish or enhance worker autonomy and self-efficacy.
caveat: Most research on algorithmic fairness and perceptions comes almost exclusively from Western-democratic contexts.
caption:
Your sense of personal agency is being reshaped by automated systems. 

Research shows a complex duality: while algorithmic management is often used for control and linked to burnout, specific designs can actually improve worker satisfaction and self-efficacy. Most of this research comes from Western-democratic contexts.

How does your work software change the way you feel about your own skills?
